page.text:
To construct a universe of sets, the deductive machinery must possess an
initial seed—an object upon which subsequent operations can act. The
simplest imaginable set is the one having no members whatsoever: the
*empty set*, denoted $\emptyset$. The Axiom of the Empty Set guarantees
that such a set exists, while the Axiom of Extensionality ensures that it
is unique. In the cumulative hierarchy of sets, the empty set serves as
the absolute base layer $V_0 = \emptyset$ from which all higher sets are
iteratively generated.
